# ALL MCP — every server in ZYRAXON

<!-- Generated by scripts/build-all-mcp.mjs. Do not edit by hand. -->

Every MCP server this product can connect, in one file. **8,202 servers in total** — 8,094 verified from the public registry and 108 curated by hand.

The two catalogs answer different questions and both ship:

- **Verified** (8,094) — produced by three generator scripts from a registry snapshot and two live passes. Each row answered a real MCP handshake or was measured to a stated depth, so a card here can be pressed and connected.
- **Curated** (108) — hand-written entries with a description, setup steps and a guide. They cover the apps most people actually want first, and a handful of them overlap the verified list by name.

#### Linear

- **id** — `linear`
- **Category** — Project
- **Kind** — `oauth`
- **Endpoint** — https://mcp.linear.app/mcp
- **Developer console** — https://linear.app/settings/api

Issues, projects and cycles

How to connect it:

1. Open https://linear.app/settings/api and press Create API key.
2. Linear accepts a redirect of http://127.0.0.1:19876/oauth/callback for its own MCP.
3. Copy the key into the Client ID field here and press Connect.

#### Atlassian

- **id** — `atlassian`
- **Category** — Project
- **Kind** — `oauth`
- **Endpoint** — https://mcp.atlassian.com/v1/mcp
- **Developer console** — https://developer.atlassian.com/console/myapps/
- **OAuth endpoints** — authorization `https://auth.atlassian.com/authorize`, token `https://auth.atlassian.com/oauth/token`

Jira issues and Confluence pages

> Atlassian scopes its MCP to one site, so an account with no site — or one that is not an admin of it — is refused after signing in.

How to connect it:

1. Open https://developer.atlassian.com/console/myapps/ and press Create.
2. Choose OAuth 2.0 integration and fill in the name and the URL of your own site.
3. Under OAuth configuration, add http://127.0.0.1:19876/oauth/callback as the callback URL and select the scopes below.
4. Copy the Client ID and the Secret into the two fields here, then press Connect.

#### Slack

- **id** — `slack`
- **Category** — Communication
- **Kind** — `oauth`
- **Endpoint** — https://mcp.slack.com/mcp
- **Developer console** — https://api.slack.com/apps
- **OAuth endpoints** — authorization `https://slack.com/oauth/v2_user/authorize`, token `https://slack.com/api/oauth.v2.user.access`
- **Default scope** — `channels:read channels:write channels:manage bookmarks:read bookmarks:write chats:read chats:write dnd:read dnd:write emoji:read files:read files:write groups:read groups:write im:history im:read im:write mpim:history mpim:read mpim:write reactions:read reactions:write search:read search:write team:read user:read user:write userprofile:read users:read users:write`

Channels, messages and files

> Slack only trusts OAuth apps a workspace owner created, so a client ID is required.

How to connect it:

1. Open https://api.slack.com/apps and press Create New App → From scratch.
2. Give it any name. Under OAuth & Permissions, add the redirect URL http://127.0.0.1:19876/oauth/callback exactly as written.
3. Open the Scopes tab and add the scopes listed below, one per line.
4. Press OAuth & Permissions → Create an App at the top. The Client ID and Client Secret appear.
5. Paste the Client ID into the field here, and the Secret into the one below it.
6. Press Connect. ZYRAXON opens Slack, you choose the workspace, and it is done.

#### Gmail

- **id** — `gmail`
- **Category** — Communication
- **Kind** — `oauth`
- **Endpoint** — https://gmailmcp.googleapis.com/mcp/v1
- **Where to get a token** — https://console.cloud.google.com/apis/credentials
- **Developer console** — https://console.cloud.google.com/apis/credentials
- **Operated by** — google

Read, search and send mail

How to connect it:

1. Open https://console.cloud.google.com/apis/credentials and pick the Google Cloud project you want to use.
2. Press Create credentials → OAuth client ID. Choose Web application as the type.
3. Under Authorized redirect URIs add http://127.0.0.1:19876/oauth/callback exactly as written, then press Create.
4. Google shows the Client ID and Client secret. Copy both.
5. Paste them into the two fields here and press Connect. Google MCP does not register clients by itself, so this one-time step is required.

How to connect it:

1. Open https://developers.facebook.com/apps and create an app of type Business.
2. Add the Instagram Graph API product and connect your Instagram Business account.
3. In Graph API Explorer generate a token with instagram_basic, instagram_content_publish, instagram_manage_comments, instagram_manage_messages and instagram_manage_insights.
4. Read your Instagram Business account id from the same explorer, then paste both values here and press Connect.

#### WhatsApp

- **id** — `whatsapp`
- **Category** — Communication
- **Kind** — `local`
- **Start command** — `npx -y @sjawhar/whatsapp-mcp`

Read chats, send text, media and voice, manage contacts

How to connect it:

1. Start the WhatsApp server — npx -y @sjawhar/whatsapp-mcp in a terminal, or press Connect here.
2. Watch the terminal: on first run it prints a QR code (the MCP channel stays clean because the QR goes to stderr).
3. On your phone open WhatsApp → Settings → Linked devices → Link a device and scan the QR.
4. The server reports Authenticated as <your name> on success. It remembers the session, so later starts need no QR.
5. The session lives in the folder you start it from: auth_info/ holds the login, data/ the SQLite copy of your chats. Back up auth_info/ to skip the QR next time, and delete it to force a fresh scan.
6. To send a file it has to sit in uploads/ (ALLOWED_SEND_DIR) — the server refuses paths outside it. Sending, deleting a message and deleting a chat each ask for confirmation before they act.

required for every protected deployment<br>`DATAPRISM_SECURITY_JWT_AUDIENCE` — Expected JWT audience claim for this deployment; required for every protected deployment<br>`DATAPRISM_SECURITY_JWT_JWK_SET_URI` — HTTPS JWKS location used to verify caller JWTs; exactly one of this or DATAPRISM_SECURITY_JWT_ISSUER_DISCOVERY_URI is required, never both<br>`DATAPRISM_SECURITY_CALLER_CLAIMS_PRINCIPAL` — JWT claim name that carries the caller's principal identifier; required, must differ from the roles and investigation claims<br>`DATAPRISM_SECURITY_CALLER_CLAIMS_ROLES` — JWT claim name that carries the caller's roles; required, must differ from the principal and investigation claims<br>`DATAPRISM_SECURITY_CALLER_CLAIMS_INVESTIGATION` — JWT claim name that carries the trusted investigation/case identifier; required, must differ from the principal and roles claims<br>`DATAPRISM_SECURITY_POLICY_PURPOSES` — Comma-separated list of permitted purposes; at least one is required<br>`DATAPRISM_SECURITYPOLICY_ROLES_INVESTIGATOR` — Example only — declare DATAPRISM_SECURITYPOLICY_ROLES_<ROLE> per operator-defined role (no underscore between SECURITY and POLICY: Spring Boot's map-key enumeration under a hyphenated dataprism.security-policy.roles.<role> segment only binds the concatenated prefix, verified by binding this property directly against Spring Boot 4.1.1), a comma-separated list of known MCP tool capabilities; at least one role-to-capability mapping is required<br>`DATAPRISM_PRIVACY_PROFILE` — Name of the reviewed privacy profile implementation to apply; required<br>`DATAPRISM_PRIVACY_SCOPE_LIFETIME` — Positive duration (e.g. 8h) a privacy scope's synthetic identities remain valid; required<br>`DATAPRISM_PRIVACY_HMAC_KEY_KEY_ID` — Identifier of the pinned HMAC key used to derive synthetic identities; required<br>`DATAPRISM_PRIVACY_HMAC_KEY_ENVIRONMENT_VARIABLE` — Name of the environment variable holding the HMAC key material; exactly one of this or DATAPRISM_PRIVACY_HMAC_KEY_PROVIDER_REFERENCE is required, never both, and never a literal key value<br>`DATAPRISM_AUDIT_SINK` — Audit sink implementation: one of approved-sink, slf4j, hash-chained; required, never downgraded to no-op<br>`DATAPRISM_AUDIT_WRITER_ID` — Writer/instance identity recorded on every audit entry; required<br>`DATAPRISM_METRICS_SINK` — Metrics sink binding, currently only micrometer; required in production, never the framework no-op<br>`DATAPRISM_HAZELCAST_TOPOLOGY` — Cluster read-budget topology: embedded (shared across members that have joined one cluster; set cluster name and join mode) or single-node (enforced per process); required, never defaulted<br>`DATAPRISM_SOURCES_CUSTOMER_BASE_URL` — Example only — declare DATAPRISM_SOURCES_<NAME>_BASE_URL (HTTPS) per configured source; at least one source, each with its own reviewed DataSourceAdapter bean, is required<br>`DATAPRISM_SOURCES_CUSTOMER_TIMEOUT` — Example only — declare DATAPRISM_SOURCES_<NAME>_TIMEOUT (positive duration) per configured source; required alongside its base URL<br>console: https://aindriub.github.io/data-prism/ |

## How to regenerate this file

```
bun run "MCP Hub/scripts/build-all-mcp.mjs"
```

The generator reads `catalog/verified-index.ts`, `catalog/connect-detail.ts` and `catalog/seed.ts` and writes this file. It needs no network and no credentials.
